audioNotice: audioEligible is packaged false because AUDIO_NOT_AUTHORIZED requires an approved owning pattern. All 224 examples remain future pronunciation-playback candidates and become eligible only after product approval, exactly as the released 45 did at Priority 8 Phase 1A. This authorizes no Listening.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: brać udział w + Locative is a fixed expression meaning to take part in something; udział is a fixed word here, not a replaceable object: biorę udział w konferencji (I'm taking part in the conference).
rows.exampleEn: I'm taking part in the conference.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The thing taken takes the Accusative; you can optionally add the Instrumental for what it's taken with: biorę kostki lodu szczypcami (I pick up ice cubes with tongs).
rows.exampleEn: I pick up ice cubes with tongs.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: To take hold of someone or something by a part, use Accusative + za + Accusative for the gripped part, both required: biorę dziecko za rękę (I'm taking the child by the hand).
rows.exampleEn: I'm taking the child by the hand.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The desired thing takes the Genitive; you can optionally add od + Genitive for who it's wanted from, or dla + Genitive for who it's wanted for: chcę pomocy od brata (I want help from my brother).
rows.exampleEn: I want help from my brother.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use an infinitive for what you yourself want to do: chcę zwiedzić Kraków (I want to visit Krakow).
rows.exampleEn: I want to visit Krakow.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use żeby to say you want something to happen, done by someone or something else: chcę, żeby dzieci były szczęśliwe (I want the children to be happy).
rows.exampleEn: I want the children to be happy.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use the first-person conditional chciałbym/chciałabym for a polite request, with the requested thing in the Accusative — not ordinary present-tense chcę: chciałbym herbatę (I would like a tea).
rows.exampleEn: I would like a tea.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use chciałbym/chciałabym plus an infinitive for a polite stated intention: chciałbym zapytać o rezerwację (I would like to ask about a reservation).
rows.exampleEn: I would like to ask about a reservation.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use chciałbym/chciałabym with żeby for a polite request directed at someone else's action: chciałbym, żebyś do mnie zadzwonił (I would like you to call me).
rows.exampleEn: I would like you to call me.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For a regular activity or class, use na + Accusative: chodzę na kurs polskiego (I go to a Polish course). This is not just a spatial destination.
rows.exampleEn: I go to a Polish course.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For regular trips on foot, do + Genitive can name a selected destination; other destination prepositions are possible in other contexts.
rows.exampleEn: I go to the library regularly.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use an infinitive to say the activity you go to do regularly: chodzę pływać (I go swimming).
rows.exampleEn: I go swimming.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For a nominal cause or object of satisfaction, use the bare Instrumental: cieszę się zaufaniem zespołu (I enjoy the team's trust).
rows.exampleEn: I enjoy the team's trust.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For an occasion you're looking forward to, use na + Accusative: cieszę się na wakacje (I'm looking forward to the holidays).
rows.exampleEn: I'm looking forward to the holidays.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For an existing or already-received source of joy, use z + Genitive: cieszę się z twojego sukcesu (I'm happy about your success).
rows.exampleEn: I'm happy about your success.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For a propositional cause, add a że clause: cieszę się, że przyjechałeś (I'm happy that you came).
rows.exampleEn: I'm happy that you came.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: What is read takes the Accusative; you can optionally add the Dative for who it's read to: czytam dzieciom książkę (I'm reading the children a book).
rows.exampleEn: I'm reading the children a book.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: You can also read exact words aloud directly, optionally naming who you're reading to with the Dative: czytam dzieciom: „Ala ma kota” (I'm reading to the children: "Ala has a cat.").
rows.exampleEn: I'm reading to the children: "Ala has a cat."

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use a question word to introduce read content: czytam, dlaczego ceny rosną (I'm reading why prices are rising).
rows.exampleEn: I'm reading why prices are rising.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: To read about a topic, use o + Locative, which is required here: czytam o polityce (I'm reading about politics). This names the topic you're reading about, not a location.
rows.exampleEn: I'm reading about politics.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use że to introduce what you read as a clause: czytam, że ceny rosną (I'm reading that prices are rising).
rows.exampleEn: I'm reading that prices are rising.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The thing given takes the Accusative and the recipient takes the Dative, and both are required: dałem sąsiadowi klucze (I gave the neighbor the keys).
rows.exampleEn: I gave the neighbor the keys.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The thing given takes the Accusative and the recipient takes the Dative, and both are required: daję sąsiadowi klucze (I'm giving the neighbor the keys).
rows.exampleEn: I'm giving the neighbor the keys.

glossesEn: get to a destination by vehicle
rows.learnerExplanationEn: For reaching an endpoint by transport, do + Genitive is one way to name it; it is not the only possible endpoint preposition.
rows.exampleEn: We will get to the hotel.

glossesEn: get to a destination by vehicle
rows.learnerExplanationEn: When you name the vehicle used to reach the endpoint, use the bare Instrumental: dojadę pociągiem (I'll get there by train).
rows.exampleEn: I will get there by train.

glossesEn: get to a destination by vehicle
rows.learnerExplanationEn: For reaching an endpoint by transport, na + Accusative is another way to name it; other endpoint prepositions are possible.
rows.exampleEn: We will get to the station.

glossesEn: get to a destination by vehicle
rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use na + Locative for reaching the endpoint on a vehicle or piece of equipment: dojedziemy na rowerach (we'll get there by bicycle).
rows.exampleEn: We will get there by bicycle.

glossesEn: arrive at a truth or conviction
rows.learnerExplanationEn: For reaching a conclusion or truth, use do + Genitive: dojść do wniosku (reach a conclusion). This is not about physically walking somewhere.
rows.exampleEn: We reached a conclusion.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use do + Genitive for who you're calling — a documented target realization, not exclusive government: dzwonię do mamy (I'm calling my mom).
rows.exampleEn: I'm calling my mom.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use na + Accusative for an institution or number you're calling — another documented target realization: dzwonię na policję (I'm calling the police).
rows.exampleEn: I'm calling the police.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use że to report what you're calling to say: dzwonię, że się spóźnię (I'm calling to say I'll be late).
rows.exampleEn: I'm calling to say I'll be late.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use żeby to request an action: dzwonię, żebyś odebrał paczkę (I'm calling to ask you to pick up the package).
rows.exampleEn: I'm calling to ask you to pick up the package.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Both the prepared dish (Accusative) and the person it's for (Dative) are optional and can be named together or left out: gotuję obiad mamie (I'm cooking dinner for my mom).
rows.exampleEn: I'm cooking dinner for my mom.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For this journey on foot, do + Genitive is one common way to name the destination; other destinations use other prepositions.
rows.exampleEn: I am going to the shop.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use an infinitive to say the action you are going to do: idę kupić chleb (I'm going to buy bread).
rows.exampleEn: I am going to buy bread.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For this journey on foot, na + Accusative is another way to name the destination; it does not replace other destination prepositions.
rows.exampleEn: I am going to the swimming pool.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For this journey by transport, do + Genitive is one way to name the selected destination; it is not the only possible destination preposition.
rows.exampleEn: I am travelling to Gdańsk.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: When you name the vehicle, use the bare Instrumental: jadę autobusem (I'm travelling by bus). In this sense it names the selected vehicle for the journey.
rows.exampleEn: I am travelling by bus.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use na + Locative for travel on a vehicle or piece of equipment: jadę na rowerze (I'm travelling by bicycle).
rows.exampleEn: I am travelling by bicycle.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Both parts are optional: the food takes the Accusative and the implement the Instrumental — dziecko je zupę łyżką (the child eats the soup with a spoon) — or just je (is eating). Jeść has no Genitive object of its own.
rows.exampleEn: The child is eating the soup with a spoon.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For repeated travel by transport, do + Genitive can name a selected destination; other destination prepositions are possible in other contexts.
rows.exampleEn: I travel to Gdynia.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: When you name the vehicle for repeated travel, use the bare Instrumental: jeżdżę tramwajem (I travel by tram). This is a selected vehicle pattern, not a frequency pattern.
rows.exampleEn: I travel by tram.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use na + Locative for repeated travel on a vehicle or piece of equipment: jeżdżę na nartach (I go skiing).
rows.exampleEn: I go skiing.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use a dependent question clause when the disputed point is an open question. For a yes/no question that word is czy: kłócimy się, czy powinniśmy wyjechać (we're arguing about whether we should leave); question words such as gdzie or kiedy work the same way.
rows.exampleEn: We're arguing about whether we should leave.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For the topic of the argument, use o + Accusative: kłócimy się o drobiazgi (we argue about trivial things). A plural subject like this doesn't need a separate z-phrase.
rows.exampleEn: We argue about trivial things.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For who you're arguing with, use z + Instrumental: kłócę się z bratem (I argue with my brother).
rows.exampleEn: I argue with my brother.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use że to introduce the topic as a clause: kłócimy się, że nikt nie sprząta (we argue that nobody cleans up).
rows.examplePl: Kłócimy się, że nikt nie sprząta.
rows.exampleEn: We argue that nobody cleans up.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The same Accusative shape covers a deep attachment to a place, a country or an ideal: kocham swoje rodzinne miasto (I love my home town). This is emotional attachment, not just liking something.
rows.exampleEn: I love my home town.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For loving a person, kochać takes a plain Accusative object: kocham swoją babcię (I love my grandmother).
rows.exampleEn: I love my grandmother very much.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Kochać also expresses a strong everyday preference for a thing, like English I love chocolate: moja siostra kocha czekoladę.
rows.exampleEn: My sister loves chocolate.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For an activity you love doing, use a bare infinitive: dzieci kochają biegać po plaży (the children love running on the beach). Only this liking sense takes an infinitive.
rows.exampleEn: The children love running on the beach.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The task you finish takes the Accusative: kończę pracę (I'm finishing the work).
rows.exampleEn: I am finishing the work.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use an infinitive to say what you're finishing doing: kończę czytać książkę (I'm finishing reading the book).
rows.exampleEn: I am finishing reading the book.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The same z + Genitive also covers taking advantage of something that benefits you, such as a discount or an opportunity: studenci korzystają ze zniżek (students take advantage of discounts).
rows.examplePl: Studenci chętnie korzystają ze zniżek studenckich.
rows.exampleEn: Students readily take advantage of student discounts.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For using a resource, service or facility, korzystać takes z + Genitive: korzystam z komunikacji miejskiej (I use public transport).
rows.exampleEn: I use public transport every day.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: To say who benefits, one way is the Dative: kupiłem jej kwiaty (I bought her flowers).
rows.exampleEn: I bought her flowers.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Another way to say who benefits is dla + Genitive: kupiłem prezenty dla całej rodziny (I bought presents for the whole family).
rows.exampleEn: I bought presents for the whole family.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: You can add who you bought from with od + Genitive and the price with za + Accusative: kupię chleb od piekarza za pięć złotych (I will buy bread from a baker for five złoty).
rows.examplePl: Kupię chleb od piekarza za pięć złotych.
rows.exampleEn: I will buy bread from a baker for five złoty.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: To say who benefits, one way is the Dative: kupuję dzieciom zabawki (I buy the children toys).
rows.exampleEn: I buy the children toys.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Another way to say who benefits is dla + Genitive: kupuję zabawki dla dzieci (I buy toys for the children).
rows.exampleEn: I buy toys for the children.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: You can add who you buy from with od + Genitive and the price with za + Accusative: kupuję warzywa od rolnika za dziesięć złotych (I buy vegetables from a farmer for ten złoty).
rows.examplePl: Kupuję warzywa od rolnika za dziesięć złotych.
rows.exampleEn: I buy vegetables from a farmer for ten złoty.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For the cause of your worry, use the bare Instrumental: martwię się twoim zdrowiem (I'm worried about your health).
rows.exampleEn: I'm worried about your health.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For an uncertain worrying question, add an embedded question: martwię się, jak sobie poradzimy (I'm worried about how we'll manage).
rows.exampleEn: I'm worried about how we'll manage.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For the person or thing you're concerned about, use o + Accusative: martwię się o egzamin (I'm worried about the exam).
rows.exampleEn: I'm worried about the exam.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For a worrying fact or possibility, add a że clause: martwię się, że się spóźnimy (I'm worried that we'll be late).
rows.exampleEn: I'm worried that we'll be late.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use w + Locative for where you live — a documented residence-place realization, not the only possible form; add z + Instrumental for a co-resident you live with: mieszkam w Warszawie z bratem (I live in Warsaw with my brother).
rows.exampleEn: I live in Warsaw with my brother.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For what you're able to do, use a bare infinitive: mogę podnieść tę walizkę (I can lift this suitcase).
rows.exampleEn: I can lift this suitcase.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For what you're allowed to do, use the same bare-infinitive shape; a permission request is just this construction asked as a question: czy mogę otworzyć okno? (may I open the window?).
rows.exampleEn: May I open the window?

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Musieć always takes a bare infinitive: muszę iść do lekarza (I have to go to the doctor). This is the only construction it uses.
rows.exampleEn: I have to go to the doctor today.

glossesEn: be a member of a group or organization
rows.learnerExplanationEn: For the group you belong to, use do + Genitive: należę do klubu sportowego (I belong to a sports club).
rows.exampleEn: I belong to a sports club.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For who owns something, use do + Genitive: ten dom należy do sąsiadki (this house belongs to my neighbor).
rows.exampleEn: This house belongs to my neighbor.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: What you write takes the Accusative: napisałem powieść (I wrote a novel).
rows.exampleEn: I wrote a novel.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: What you write takes the Accusative; the bare Dative recipient is optional here: napisałem koledze wiadomość (I wrote my friend a message).
rows.exampleEn: I wrote my friend a message.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: You can write exact words directly; the bare Dative recipient is optional here: napisałem koledze: „Wracam jutro” (I wrote to my friend: "I'm coming back tomorrow.").
rows.exampleEn: I wrote to my friend: "I'm coming back tomorrow."

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use a question word to introduce written content. The bare Dative recipient is REQUIRED in this clause alternative: napisałem koledze, o której wrócę (I wrote to my friend what time I'll be back).
rows.exampleEn: I wrote to my friend what time I'll be back.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For the topic you're writing about, use o + Locative, which is required here; the bare Dative recipient is optional in this alternative: napisałem koledze o wakacjach (I wrote my friend about the holidays).
rows.exampleEn: I wrote my friend about the holidays.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use że to introduce what you wrote as a clause. Unlike pisać, in this clause alternative the bare Dative recipient is REQUIRED, not optional: napisałem koledze, że wrócę jutro (I wrote to my friend that I'll be back tomorrow).
rows.exampleEn: I wrote to my friend that I'll be back tomorrow.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use żeby to introduce what you're asking someone to do. The bare Dative recipient is REQUIRED in this clause alternative: napisałem koledze, żeby zadzwonił (I wrote my friend, asking him to call).
rows.exampleEn: I wrote my friend, asking him to call.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: What you write takes the Accusative; do + Genitive for the recipient remains optional here: napisałem do koleżanki wiadomość (I wrote a message to my friend).
rows.exampleEn: I wrote a message to my friend.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: You can write exact words directly; do + Genitive for the recipient remains optional here: napisałem do koleżanki: „Wracam jutro” (I wrote to my friend: "I'm coming back tomorrow.").
rows.exampleEn: I wrote to my friend: "I'm coming back tomorrow."

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use a question word to introduce written content; do + Genitive for the recipient remains optional here: napisałem do koleżanki, o której wrócę (I wrote to my friend what time I'll be back).
rows.examplePl: Napisałem do koleżanki, o której wrócę.
rows.exampleEn: I wrote to my friend what time I'll be back.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For the topic you're writing about, use o + Locative, which is required here; do + Genitive for the recipient stays optional throughout, unlike Dative on the clause alternatives: napisałem do koleżanki o wakacjach (I wrote to my friend about the holidays).
rows.exampleEn: I wrote to my friend about the holidays.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use że to introduce what you wrote as a clause; do + Genitive for the recipient remains optional here: napisałem do koleżanki, że wracam jutro (I wrote to my friend that I'm coming back tomorrow).
rows.examplePl: Napisałem do koleżanki, że wracam jutro.
rows.exampleEn: I wrote to my friend that I'm coming back tomorrow.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use żeby to introduce what you're asking someone to do; do + Genitive for the recipient remains optional here: napisałem do koleżanki, żeby zadzwoniła (I wrote to my friend, asking her to call).
rows.exampleEn: I wrote to my friend, asking her to call.

glossesEn: view something all the way through
rows.learnerExplanationEn: What you watched takes the Accusative: obejrzałem ten film (I watched that movie).
rows.exampleEn: I watched that movie.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: You can also give the answer's exact words directly: odpowiadam: „Nie wiem” (I answer: "I don't know").
rows.exampleEn: I answer: "I don't know."

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For what you're answering, use na + Accusative: odpowiadam na pytanie (I'm answering the question).
rows.exampleEn: I am answering the question.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use że to introduce the content of your answer: odpowiadam, że nie wiem (I answer that I don't know).
rows.exampleEn: I answer that I don't know.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The person or content you watch takes the Accusative; you can optionally add w + Locative for the film/show they appear in — not the TV or place you're watching from: oglądam ją w nowym serialu (I'm watching her in a new series).
rows.exampleEn: I'm watching her in a new series.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use an infinitive when you and the person doing the action are the same: pamiętaj zamknąć drzwi (remember to close the door).
rows.exampleEn: Remember to close the door.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use żeby when the person who should act is different: pamiętaj, żeby dzieci umyły ręce (remember that the children should wash their hands).
rows.exampleEn: Remember that the children should wash their hands.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The thing you remember takes the Accusative: pamiętam ten dzień (I remember that day).
rows.exampleEn: I remember that day.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For a remembered topic, use o + Locative: pamiętam o twoich urodzinach (I remember your birthday).
rows.exampleEn: I remember your birthday.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For an appearance/character match, use do + Genitive: ten krawat pasuje do garnituru (this tie matches the suit).
rows.exampleEn: This tie matches the suit.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Name whose expectations are or aren't satisfied with an optional Dative: ten termin mi nie pasuje (this date doesn't suit me).
rows.exampleEn: This date doesn't suit me.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For a physical fit by size/shape, do + Genitive is one optional target form: ten klucz pasuje do zamka (this key fits the lock).
rows.exampleEn: This key fits the lock.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: na + Accusative is the alternative optional target form for a physical fit: ten pierścionek pasuje na mój palec (this ring fits my finger).
rows.examplePl: Ten pierścionek pasuje na mój palec.
rows.exampleEn: This ring fits my finger.

glossesEn: be typical of/appropriate for someone or something
rows.learnerExplanationEn: do + Genitive names what something is being compared against; adding a Dative optionally names whose judgment it is: ten kolor mi do ciebie nie pasuje (I don't think this color suits you).
rows.examplePl: Ten kolor mi do ciebie nie pasuje.
rows.exampleEn: I don't think this color suits you.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The drink goes in the Accusative: piję kawę (I drink coffee). Keep this everyday drinking sense apart from pić used for drinking alcohol.
rows.exampleEn: I drink coffee every morning.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: What you write takes the Accusative: piszę powieść (I'm writing a novel).
rows.exampleEn: I'm writing a novel.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: What you write takes the Accusative; you can optionally add the bare Dative for who you're writing to: piszę koledze wiadomość (I'm writing my friend a message).
rows.exampleEn: I'm writing my friend a message.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: You can write exact words directly; you can optionally add the bare Dative for who you're writing to: piszę koledze: „Wracam jutro” (I'm writing to my friend: "I'm coming back tomorrow.").
rows.exampleEn: I'm writing to my friend: "I'm coming back tomorrow."

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use a question word to introduce written content; you can optionally add the bare Dative for who you're writing to: piszę koledze, o której wrócę (I'm writing to my friend what time I'll be back).
rows.exampleEn: I'm writing to my friend what time I'll be back.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For the topic you're writing about, use o + Locative, which is required here; you can optionally add the Dative for who you're writing to (no preposition): piszę koledze o wakacjach (I'm writing my friend about the holidays).
rows.exampleEn: I'm writing my friend about the holidays.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use że to introduce what you're writing as a clause; you can optionally add the bare Dative for who you're writing to: piszę koledze, że wracam jutro (I'm writing to my friend that I'll be back tomorrow).
rows.exampleEn: I'm writing to my friend that I'll be back tomorrow.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use żeby to introduce what you're asking someone to do; you can optionally add the bare Dative for who you're writing to: piszę koledze, żeby zadzwonił (I'm writing my friend, asking him to call).
rows.exampleEn: I'm writing my friend, asking him to call.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: What you write takes the Accusative; you can optionally add do + Genitive for who you're writing to: piszę do koleżanki wiadomość (I'm writing a message to my friend).
rows.exampleEn: I'm writing a message to my friend.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: You can write exact words directly; you can optionally add do + Genitive for who you're writing to: piszę do koleżanki: „Wracam jutro” (I'm writing to my friend: "I'm coming back tomorrow.").
rows.exampleEn: I'm writing to my friend: "I'm coming back tomorrow."

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use a question word to introduce written content; you can optionally add do + Genitive for who you're writing to: piszę do koleżanki, o której wrócę (I'm writing to my friend what time I'll be back).
rows.examplePl: Piszę do koleżanki, o której wrócę.
rows.exampleEn: I'm writing to my friend what time I'll be back.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For the topic you're writing about, use o + Locative, which is required here; you can optionally add do + Genitive (literally 'to') for who you're writing to: piszę do koleżanki o wakacjach (I'm writing to my friend about the holidays).
rows.exampleEn: I'm writing to my friend about the holidays.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use że to introduce what you're writing as a clause; you can optionally add do + Genitive for who you're writing to: piszę do koleżanki, że wracam jutro (I'm writing to my friend that I'm coming back tomorrow).
rows.examplePl: Piszę do koleżanki, że wracam jutro.
rows.exampleEn: I'm writing to my friend that I'm coming back tomorrow.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use żeby to introduce what you're asking someone to do; you can optionally add do + Genitive for who you're writing to: piszę do koleżanki, żeby zadzwoniła (I'm writing to my friend, asking her to call).
rows.exampleEn: I'm writing to my friend, asking her to call.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The person you show something to takes the Dative, and the thing shown takes the Accusative: pokazuję dzieciom zdjęcia (I'm showing the children photos).
rows.exampleEn: I'm showing the children photos.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use a question word to introduce shown content: pokazuję, jak to zrobić (I show how to do it).
rows.exampleEn: I show how to do it.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: To point at or toward something, use na + Accusative: pokazuję na mapę (I'm pointing at the map).
rows.exampleEn: I'm pointing at the map.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The Accusative names the ordered action as a noun (usually a gerund/action noun), not a recommended item: trener poleca zawodnikom rozgrzewkę (the coach instructs the players to warm up).
rows.exampleEn: The coach instructs the players to warm up.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: An instruction can also be quoted directly: kierownik poleca mi: „Zamknij drzwi” (the manager tells me: "Close the door.").
rows.exampleEn: The manager tells me: "Close the door."

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For an instruction to act, use a bare infinitive; naming who is instructed (Dative) is optional: lekarz poleca mi odpoczywać (the doctor tells me to rest).
rows.exampleEn: The doctor tells me to rest.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: A żeby clause is another way to give the same instruction: szef poleca mi, żebym przygotował raport (my boss tells me to prepare the report).
rows.examplePl: Szef poleca mi, żebym przygotował raport.
rows.exampleEn: My boss tells me to prepare the report.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Name the recommended person or item with the Accusative; the recipient (Dative) is optional: polecam ci tę restaurację (I recommend this restaurant to you).
rows.exampleEn: I recommend this restaurant to you.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: What you said takes the Accusative; you can optionally add the bare Dative for who you told: powiedziałem koledze prawdę (I told my friend the truth).
rows.exampleEn: I told my friend the truth.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use a question word to introduce what you said; you can optionally add the bare Dative for who you told: powiedziałem koledze, o której wracam (I told my friend what time I'm coming back).
rows.exampleEn: I told my friend what time I'm coming back.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use o + Locative for the topic you told someone about, which is required here; the bare Dative recipient is optional: powiedziałem koledze o problemie (I told my friend about the problem).
rows.exampleEn: I told my friend about the problem.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use że to introduce what you said as a clause; you can optionally add the bare Dative for who you told: powiedziałem koledze, że wyjeżdżam (I told my friend that I'm leaving).
rows.exampleEn: I told my friend that I'm leaving.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use żeby to introduce what you asked someone to do; you can optionally add the bare Dative for who you told: powiedziałem koledze, żeby poczekał (I told my friend to wait).
rows.exampleEn: I told my friend to wait.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: You can report exact spoken words directly, with no recipient in this schema: powiedziałem: „Zaraz wracam” (I said: "I'll be right back.").
rows.exampleEn: I said: "I'll be right back."

rows.learnerExplanationEn: What you said takes the Accusative; you can optionally add do + Genitive for who you told: powiedziałem do koleżanki prawdę (I told the truth to my friend).
rows.exampleEn: I told the truth to my friend.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use a question word to introduce what you said; you can optionally add do + Genitive for who you told: powiedziałem do koleżanki, o której wracam (I mentioned to my friend what time I'm coming back).
rows.examplePl: Powiedziałem do koleżanki, o której wracam.
rows.exampleEn: I mentioned to my friend what time I'm coming back.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use o + Locative for the topic, which is required here; you can optionally add do + Genitive for who you told: powiedziałem do koleżanki o problemie (I mentioned the problem to my friend).
rows.exampleEn: I mentioned the problem to my friend.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use że to introduce what you said as a clause; you can optionally add do + Genitive for who you told: powiedziałem do koleżanki, że wyjeżdżam (I mentioned to my friend that I'm leaving).
rows.exampleEn: I mentioned to my friend that I'm leaving.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use żeby to introduce what you asked someone to do; you can optionally add do + Genitive for who you told: powiedziałem do koleżanki, żeby poczekała (I told my friend to wait).
rows.exampleEn: I told my friend to wait.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: You can name who is allowed with the Dative, then say what with na + Accusative: mama pozwala mi na wyjście (Mom allows me to go out).
rows.exampleEn: Mom allows me to go out.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use żeby when the permitted person is the subject of their own clause: mama pozwala, żeby dzieci oglądały bajki (Mom allows the children to watch cartoons).
rows.examplePl: Mama pozwala, żeby dzieci oglądały bajki.
rows.exampleEn: Mom allows the children to watch cartoons.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: A standalone infinitive gives general permission without naming a person: pozwalam pracować z domu (I allow working from home).
rows.exampleEn: I allow working from home.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: An infinitive can also follow directly: internet pozwala pracować zdalnie (the internet allows working remotely).
rows.exampleEn: The internet allows working remotely.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For a thing or situation making something possible, use na + Accusative: internet pozwala na szybką komunikację (the internet allows quick communication).
rows.exampleEn: The internet allows quick communication.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: A żeby-clause can follow when the enabling thing is more abstract, such as a law or policy: prawo pozwala, żeby firmy stosowały ulgi (the law allows companies to apply tax breaks).
rows.examplePl: Prawo pozwala, żeby firmy stosowały ulgi.
rows.exampleEn: The law allows companies to apply tax breaks.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For creating or developing something, use nad + Instrumental: pracuję nad filmem (I'm working on a film).
rows.exampleEn: I am working on a new film.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The attempted result can also be a noun in the Genitive: próbuję szczęścia (I'm trying my luck).
rows.exampleEn: I'm trying my luck.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use an infinitive to say what you're trying to do: próbuję rozwiązać problem (I'm trying to solve the problem).
rows.exampleEn: I'm trying to solve the problem.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The food or drink you taste takes the Genitive: próbuję zupy (I'm tasting the soup).
rows.exampleEn: I'm tasting the soup.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Name the person in the Accusative and what you are sorry for with za + Accusative; in this pattern you need both: Marek przeprasza nauczyciela za spóźnienie (Marek apologises to the teacher for being late).
rows.exampleEn: Marek apologises to the teacher for being late.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: You can also explain yourself with a że clause, and here the person is optional: przepraszam cię, że nie zadzwoniłem (I apologise to you for not calling), or simply przepraszam, że nie zadzwoniłem.
rows.examplePl: Przepraszam cię, że nie zadzwoniłem wczoraj.
rows.exampleEn: I apologise to you for not calling yesterday.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: One common way to express this destination is do + Genitive: przyjadę do Warszawy (I'll arrive in Warsaw).
rows.exampleEn: I will arrive in Warsaw.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Another common way to express this destination is na + Accusative: przyjadę na dworzec (I'll arrive at the station).
rows.exampleEn: I will arrive at the station.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For literal arrival at a place, do + Genitive can name the destination; it is one way to express that destination.
rows.exampleEn: We came to the museum.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use an infinitive to say the one-off action you came to do: przyszedłem odebrać dokument (I came to collect a document).
rows.exampleEn: I came to collect a document.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For a one-off event or activity, na + Accusative can name the destination: przyszliśmy na koncert (we came to a concert).
rows.exampleEn: We came to a concert.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The thing you bring takes the Accusative: przynoszę kawę (I'm bringing coffee).
rows.exampleEn: I am bringing coffee.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Name who you're advising (Dative, required) and the advice item (Accusative): radzę ci ostrożność (I advise you to be careful).
rows.exampleEn: I advise you to be careful.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Advice can be quoted directly, with the advisee (Dative) still required: radzę ci: „Odpocznij trochę” (I advise you: "Rest a little.").
rows.exampleEn: I advise you: "Rest a little."

rows.learnerExplanationEn: With a bare infinitive, the advisee (Dative) becomes optional, unlike every other row above: radzę ci zjeść coś przed wyjściem (I advise you to eat something before leaving).
rows.examplePl: Radzę ci zjeść coś przed wyjściem.
rows.exampleEn: I advise you to eat something before leaving.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: An embedded question gives advice content, with the advisee (Dative) still required: radzę ci, jak rozwiązać ten problem (I advise you on how to solve this problem).
rows.examplePl: Radzę ci, jak rozwiązać ten problem.
rows.exampleEn: I advise you on how to solve this problem.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: A żeby clause gives the advised action, with the advisee (Dative) still required: radzę ci, żebyś odpoczął (I advise you to rest).
rows.exampleEn: I advise you to rest.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For the difficulty you're handling, use z + Instrumental: radzę sobie z trudnościami (I cope with difficulties).
rows.exampleEn: I cope with difficulties.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Name what you're booking with the Accusative; add who it's for with an optional Dative: rezerwuję stolik znajomym (I'm reserving a table for my friends).
rows.exampleEn: I'm reserving a table for my friends.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: dla + Genitive is an alternative way to name the beneficiary, never combined with the Dative form: rezerwuję pokój dla rodziców (I'm reserving a room for my parents).
rows.exampleEn: I'm reserving a room for my parents.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The named activity you perform takes the Accusative — you are not creating this thing, you are doing it: robię pranie (I'm doing the laundry).
rows.exampleEn: I'm doing the laundry.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The thing you make or create takes the Accusative: robię ciasto (I'm making a cake).
rows.exampleEn: I'm making a cake.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: What you understand takes the Accusative: rozumiem żart (I understand the joke).
rows.exampleEn: I understand the joke.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use a question word to introduce understood content: rozumiem, dlaczego się spóźniłeś (I understand why you were late).
rows.exampleEn: I understand why you were late.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use że to introduce what you understand as a clause: rozumiem, że jesteś zmęczony (I understand that you're tired).
rows.exampleEn: I understand that you're tired.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The person you empathically understand takes the Accusative: rozumiem cię jak nikt inny (I understand you like no one else).
rows.exampleEn: I understand you like no one else.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The finished task or activity takes the Accusative: skończyłem pracę (I finished the work).
rows.exampleEn: I finished the work.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use an infinitive for the activity you finished doing: skończyłem pisać raport (I finished writing the report).
rows.exampleEn: I finished writing the report.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use z + Instrumental for definitively giving up a habit or activity for good — a separate colloquial sense from finishing an ordinary task: skończyłem z paleniem (I'm done with smoking).
rows.exampleEn: I'm done with smoking.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For who you met up with, use z + Instrumental: spotkałem się z przyjaciółmi (I met up with friends). A reciprocal plural subject like 'we met' doesn't need a separate z-phrase.
rows.exampleEn: I met up with friends.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For who you meet up with, use z + Instrumental: spotykam się z przyjaciółmi (I meet up with friends). A reciprocal plural subject like 'we meet' doesn't need a separate z-phrase.
rows.exampleEn: I meet up with friends.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For teaching a school subject, the subject takes the Genitive and naming the pupils is optional: pani Nowak uczy moją córkę matematyki, or simply uczy matematyki.
rows.examplePl: Pani Nowak uczy moją córkę matematyki.
rows.exampleEn: Mrs Nowak teaches my daughter maths.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Uczyć teaches somebody something: the learner takes the Accusative and what you teach takes the Genitive — babcia uczy wnuczkę cierpliwości (grandma teaches her granddaughter patience). Note that uczyć się (to learn) is a different verb.
rows.exampleEn: Grandma teaches her granddaughter patience.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For a skill, keep the Accusative learner and add a bare infinitive: ojciec uczy syna pływać (the father is teaching his son to swim).
rows.exampleEn: The father is teaching his son to swim.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: To teach how, when or whether to do something, use a dependent question clause after the Accusative learner: instruktor uczy kursantów, jak reagować (the instructor teaches the trainees how to react).
rows.examplePl: Instruktor uczy kursantów, jak reagować w niebezpiecznej sytuacji.
rows.exampleEn: The instructor teaches the trainees how to react in a dangerous situation.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: To teach that something is the case, use a że clause after the Accusative learner: rodzice uczą dzieci, że warto mówić prawdę (parents teach their children that it's worth telling the truth).
rows.examplePl: Rodzice uczą dzieci, że warto mówić prawdę.
rows.exampleEn: Parents teach their children that it is worth telling the truth.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: To name a topic you teach about rather than a subject to be mastered, use o + Locative with an Accusative person: nauczycielka uczy uczniów o polskich zwyczajach (the teacher teaches the pupils about Polish customs).
rows.examplePl: Nauczycielka uczy uczniów o polskich zwyczajach.
rows.exampleEn: The teacher teaches the pupils about Polish customs.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use do + Genitive for the venue or service you've made an appointment at — a documented realization, not the only possible location form; you can optionally add z + Instrumental for who you arranged it with: umówiłem się z żoną do lekarza (I made an appointment with my wife at the doctor's).
rows.examplePl: Umówiłem się z żoną do lekarza.
rows.exampleEn: I made an appointment with my wife at the doctor's.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Both the meeting partner (z + Instrumental) and the appointment/event (na + Accusative) are optional and can be named together or omitted depending on context: umówiłem się z kolegą na kawę (I arranged to meet my friend for coffee).
rows.examplePl: Umówiłem się z kolegą na kawę.
rows.exampleEn: I arranged to meet my friend for coffee.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use a question word to introduce what was agreed; you can optionally add z + Instrumental for who you agreed with: umówiłem się z zespołem, kto za co odpowiada (I agreed with the team who's responsible for what).
rows.examplePl: Umówiłem się z zespołem, kto za co odpowiada.
rows.exampleEn: I agreed with the team who's responsible for what.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use na + Accusative for the term you agreed on; you can optionally add z + Instrumental for who you agreed with: umówiłem się z szefem na podwyżkę (I agreed with my boss on a raise).
rows.examplePl: Umówiłem się z szefem na podwyżkę.
rows.exampleEn: I agreed with my boss on a raise.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use o + Accusative for the subject you agreed on; you can optionally add z + Instrumental for who you agreed with: umówiłem się ze sprzedawcą o cenę (I agreed with the seller on the price).
rows.examplePl: Umówiłem się ze sprzedawcą o cenę.
rows.exampleEn: I agreed with the seller on the price.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use że to introduce what you agreed as a clause; you can optionally add z + Instrumental for who you agreed with: umówiłem się z bratem, że pomoże mi w przeprowadzce (I agreed with my brother that he'll help me move).
rows.examplePl: Umówiłem się z bratem, że pomoże mi w przeprowadzce.
rows.exampleEn: I agreed with my brother that he'll help me move.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use żeby to introduce an agreed action; you can optionally add z + Instrumental for who you agreed with: umówiłem się z kolegą, żeby zachować to w tajemnicy (I agreed with my friend to keep it secret).
rows.examplePl: Umówiłem się z kolegą, żeby zachować to w tajemnicy.
rows.exampleEn: I agreed with my friend to keep it secret.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The thing you avoid takes the Genitive: unikam słodyczy (I avoid sweets).
rows.exampleEn: I avoid sweets.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For content you already know, wiedzieć takes an Accusative object, in practice usually a pronoun such as to, wszystko or coś: wiem to od dawna (I've known that for a long time).
rows.exampleEn: I have known that for a long time.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: When the content is an open question rather than a fact, use a dependent question clause. For a yes/no question that word is czy: nie wiem, czy zdążymy (I don't know whether we'll make it); question words such as gdzie or kiedy work the same way.
rows.examplePl: Nie wiem, czy zdążymy na pociąg.
rows.exampleEn: I don't know whether we'll make the train.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: To name the area or topic you know about, use o + Locative: wiem o twoich problemach (I know about your problems).
rows.exampleEn: I know about your problems.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use że to introduce a fact you know: wiem, że masz dużo pracy (I know that you have a lot of work).
rows.examplePl: Wiem, że masz teraz dużo pracy.
rows.exampleEn: I know that you have a lot of work right now.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For this return meaning, do + Genitive can express the place you return to. It is one realization of the return goal, not the only form.
rows.exampleEn: I am returning to the flat.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For this return meaning, z + Genitive can express the place you return from. It is one realization of the return source, not the only form.
rows.exampleEn: I am coming back from the cinema.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For this completed return, do + Genitive can express the place you return to. It is one realization of the return goal, not the only form.
rows.exampleEn: I will return to the flat.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For this completed return, z + Genitive can express the place you return from. It is one realization of the return source, not the only form.
rows.exampleEn: I came back from the cinema.

glossesEn: depart from a place by vehicle
rows.learnerExplanationEn: One common way to say where you're leaving from by transport is z + Genitive: wyjadę z miasta (I'll leave the city). This is a common realization of the source, not the only possible form. It does not name a destination.
rows.exampleEn: I will leave the city.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: One common way to name where you're going after leaving is do + Genitive: wyjdę do ogrodu (I'll go out to the garden).
rows.exampleEn: I will go out to the garden.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Another common way to name that destination is na + Accusative: wyjdę na balkon (I'll go out onto the balcony).
rows.exampleEn: I will go out onto the balcony.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: One common way to say where you're leaving from is z + Genitive: wyszedłem z domu (I left the house). This is a common realization of the source, not the only possible form.
rows.exampleEn: I left the house.

glossesEn: require conduct or a trait from someone
rows.learnerExplanationEn: The required thing takes the Genitive; you can optionally add od + Genitive for the person it's required from: szef wymaga lojalności od pracowników (the boss requires loyalty from employees).
rows.exampleEn: The boss requires loyalty from employees.

glossesEn: require conduct or a trait from someone
rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use żeby to introduce what someone is required to do; you can optionally add od + Genitive for the person it applies to: szef wymaga, żeby pracownicy przychodzili punktualnie (the boss requires that employees arrive on time).
rows.examplePl: Szef wymaga, żeby pracownicy przychodzili punktualnie.
rows.exampleEn: The boss requires that employees arrive on time.

glossesEn: make conduct or a condition necessary
rows.learnerExplanationEn: The required thing takes the Genitive; you can optionally add od + Genitive for the person or thing it's required from: wyjście z nałogu wymaga silnej woli (getting out of an addiction requires strong will).
rows.examplePl: Wyjście z nałogu wymaga silnej woli.
rows.exampleEn: Getting out of an addiction requires strong will.

glossesEn: make conduct or a condition necessary
rows.learnerExplanationEn: A żeby-clause can follow when the requiring subject is an abstract situation; you can optionally add od + Genitive for the person or thing it applies to: sytuacja wymaga, żeby wszyscy zachowali spokój (the situation requires that everyone stay calm).
rows.examplePl: Sytuacja wymaga, żeby wszyscy zachowali spokój.
rows.exampleEn: The situation requires that everyone stay calm.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The thing taken takes the Accusative; you can optionally add the Instrumental for what it's taken with: wziąłem kostkę lodu szczypcami (I picked up an ice cube with tongs).
rows.exampleEn: I picked up an ice cube with tongs.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: To take hold of someone or something by a part, use Accusative + za + Accusative for the gripped part, both required: wziąłem dziecko za rękę (I took the child by the hand).
rows.exampleEn: I took the child by the hand.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: wziąć udział w + Locative is a fixed expression meaning to enter into participation; udział is a fixed word here, not a replaceable object: wziąłem udział w konferencji (I took part in the conference).
rows.exampleEn: I took part in the conference.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The activity you start takes the Accusative: zacząłem lekcję (I started the lesson).
rows.exampleEn: I started the lesson.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use an infinitive to say what you started doing: zacząłem czytać książkę (I started reading a book).
rows.exampleEn: I started reading a book.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The thing you order takes the Accusative: zamawiam pizzę (I'm ordering a pizza).
rows.exampleEn: I am ordering a pizza.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: To say who the order is for, one way is the Dative: zamawiam mężowi prezent (I'm ordering a present for my husband).
rows.exampleEn: I am ordering a present for my husband.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Another way to say who the order is for is dla + Genitive: zamawiam prezent dla żony (I'm ordering a present for my wife).
rows.exampleEn: I am ordering a present for my wife.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: One common way to name the provider is u + Genitive: zamawiam meble u stolarza (I'm ordering furniture from a carpenter).
rows.exampleEn: I am ordering furniture from a carpenter.

glossesEn: fail to do something one should have done
rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use an infinitive to say the action you failed to do: zapominam zadzwonić (I forget to call).
rows.exampleEn: I forget to call.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The forgotten thing can also take the Accusative: zapominam tę twarz (I forget that face).
rows.exampleEn: I forget that face.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The forgotten thing can take the Genitive: zapominam numeru telefonu (I forget the phone number).
rows.exampleEn: I forget the phone number.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use a dependent question clause for a forgotten question. For a yes/no question that word is czy: zapominam, czy zamknąłem drzwi (I forget whether I locked the door); question words such as gdzie or kiedy work the same way.
rows.exampleEn: I forget whether I locked the door.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For a forgotten topic, use o + Locative: zapominam o spotkaniu (I forget about the meeting).
rows.exampleEn: I forget about the meeting.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Use że to introduce what you forget: zapominam, że mam spotkanie (I forget that I have a meeting).
rows.exampleEn: I forget that I have a meeting.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For a destination or institution, use do + Genitive instead: zapraszam cię do domu (I'm inviting you to my house).
rows.exampleEn: I'm inviting you to my house.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: For an event or activity, name who you're inviting (Accusative) and what to (na + Accusative): zapraszam cię na urodziny (I'm inviting you to my birthday party).
rows.exampleEn: I'm inviting you to my birthday party.

glossesEn: consent to a proposal or action
rows.learnerExplanationEn: Consent is often given as a short spoken reply to an offer or plan: zapytałem, czy możemy zacząć jutro. „Zgadzam się” — odpowiedział (I asked if we could start tomorrow. "I agree," he replied).
rows.examplePl: Zapytałem, czy możemy zacząć jutro. „Zgadzam się” — odpowiedział.
rows.exampleEn: I asked if we could start tomorrow. "I agree," he replied.

glossesEn: consent to a proposal or action
rows.learnerExplanationEn: For consenting to do something yourself, add a bare infinitive: zgadzam się zapłacić połowę (I agree to pay half).
rows.exampleEn: I agree to pay half.

glossesEn: consent to a proposal or action
rows.learnerExplanationEn: For the proposal or action you're agreeing to, use na + Accusative: zgadzam się na twoją propozycję (I agree to your proposal).
rows.exampleEn: I agree to your proposal.

glossesEn: consent to a proposal or action
rows.learnerExplanationEn: For consent expressed as letting someone do something, add a żeby clause: zgadzam się, żebyś został dłużej (I agree that you can stay longer).
rows.exampleEn: I agree that you can stay longer.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Agreement with an opinion is often a short spoken reply, with no partner named in this exact shape: powiedziałem, że film był świetny. „Zgadzam się” — dodała (I said the film was great. "I agree," she added).
rows.examplePl: Powiedziałem, że film był świetny. „Zgadzam się” — dodała.
rows.exampleEn: I said the film was great. "I agree," she added.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: To agree with a person or their view, use z + Instrumental: zgadzam się z tobą (I agree with you).
rows.exampleEn: I agree with you.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: Add a że clause for what you agree with; naming who you agree with (z + Instrumental) is optional: zgadzam się z nim, że to dobry pomysł (I agree with him that it's a good idea).
rows.examplePl: Zgadzam się z nim, że to dobry pomysł.
rows.exampleEn: I agree with him that it's a good idea.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: The person gets the Dative and the thing you wish them the Genitive: życzę ci zdrowia (I wish you health).
rows.exampleEn: I wish you health and happiness.

rows.learnerExplanationEn: To wish for something to happen, keep the Dative person and use a żeby clause instead of the Genitive: życzę ci, żebyś zdał egzamin (literally 'I wish for you that you pass the exam'; English usually says I hope you pass). Use one or the other, not both.
rows.examplePl: Życzę ci, żebyś zdał ten egzamin.
rows.exampleEn: I hope you pass this exam.
